tops.name: Notifications
tops.one_liner: Sends a message on the chosen channel and records it
tops.explain: I deliver each message on one of four channels: email, sms, app or chat_only. Real email goes out only when the SMTP_HOST setting exists and the address does not end in example.com. Anything else is simulated, meaning I write the message to the outbox table instead of sending it. Every message gets an outbox row marked sent, simulated or failed. If the mail server breaks, I record the failure and the queue keeps working.
tops.why: This matters because the demo has to run with no mail server and never email a stranger. Recording every message in one table lets anyone see exactly what would have been sent. Catching send errors stops one broken mail server from blocking every other message.

tops.name: Data store
tops.one_liner: One SQLite file, six tables, shared by two processes
tops.explain: I keep everything in one SQLite file, a database in a single disk file, with six tables: landlords, listings, saved_answers, questions, outbox and impressions. Two processes open that file at once: the stdio server and the web server. So I switch on WAL mode, a write-ahead log that lets reads and writes overlap. On first run I create the tables and load the seed data. Reset deletes the file plus its -wal and -shm side files.
tops.why: This matters because the chat server and the landlord page run as separate programs and must see the same questions. Without WAL, one process could block the other while it writes. Seeding on first run means the demo works with no setup.

tops.name: Seed data
tops.one_liner: Made-up Boston landlords, listings and answers for the demo
tops.explain: I ship a synthetic Boston dataset: 6 landlords, 20 listings and 23 saved answers. Every name, price and answer is made up. The neighbourhood and landmark coordinates are real, looked up in Apple Maps on 2026-11-21. Some landlords deliberately have no saved answer on topics like guarantors, sublets or tours, so the send-to-landlord path shows up in the demo. All landlord emails use example.com, a reserved domain that cannot receive mail.
tops.why: This matters because a demo needs realistic maps and distances without using any real person's data. The deliberate gaps force the demo to show the second path, where a question goes to the landlord. The example.com addresses guarantee no real inbox is ever emailed.
